claim: Antimicrobial-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes over 200,000 deaths each year.
source: Antimicrobial-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes over 200,000 deaths each year.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract without direct citation, but represents established knowledge about TB mortality.

claim: ODELAM enables rapid quantitative measures of growth kinetics in as little as 30 hrs under a wide variety of environmental conditions.
source: ODELAM enables rapid quantitative measures of growth kinetics in as little as 30 hrs under a wide variety of environmental conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing growth measurements at 30 hours.

claim: ODELAM identified ofloxacin heteroresistance and the presence of drug resistant colony forming units (CFUs) at 1 per 1000 CFUs in as little as 48 hrs.
source: ODELAM identified ofloxacin heteroresistance and the presence of drug resistant colony forming units (CFUs) at 1 per 1000 CFUs in as little as 48 hrs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the heteroresistance detection experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: In 2018, approximately 484,000 people developed multidrug-resistant tuberculosis.
source: In 2018, approximately 484,000 people developed multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and an estimated 214,000 people died from rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to WHO 2019 report.

claim: An estimated 214,000 people died from rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in 2018.
source: In 2018, approximately 484,000 people developed multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and an estimated 214,000 people died from rifampicin-resistant or multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to WHO 2019 report.

claim: Approximately 10% of all multidrug resistant tuberculosis infections are resistant to at least four commonly used anti-TB drugs.
source: Approximately 10% of all multidrug resistant tuberculosis infections are resistant to at least four commonly used anti-TB drugs (Dorman et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dorman et al., 2018.

claim: Culture-based methods for Mtb require one to four weeks to produce results.
source: In the case of Mtb, culture-based methods such as common agar plates or more advanced indicator tubes with fluorescent growth reporters are gold standards for identifying sensitivity to any antibiotic, but these testing methods require one to four weeks to produce results (Kim, 2005; Lawson et al., 2013; Kontos et al., 2004; Garrigó et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: PCR-based Gene-Xpert assay can rapidly identify antimicrobial resistant Mtb infections but requires knowledge of specific genetic markers associated with resistance.
source: Biomarker methods, such as the PCR-based Gene-Xpert assay, can rapidly identify antimicrobial resistant Mtb infections but require knowledge of specific genetic markers associated with resistance and are thus insensitive to unknown resistance mechanisms (Dorman et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dorman et al., 2018.

claim: Failure to rapidly identify and treat an antimicrobial-resistant or heteroresistant Mtb infection contributes to disease progression, treatment failure and tuberculosis relapse.
source: Failure to rapidly identify and treat an antimicrobial-resistant or heteroresistant Mtb infection contributes to disease progression, treatment failure and tuberculosis relapse (Shin et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shin et al., 2018.

claim: Microfluidic platforms provide high resolution phenotypic analysis of mycobacterial cell biology but are limited in the number of cells that can be readily observed.
source: Microfluidic platforms provide high resolution phenotypic analysis of mycobacterial cell biology but are limited in the number of cells that can be readily observed (Aldridge et al., 2012; Golchin et al., 2012; Wakamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on microfluidic platforms.

claim: Conventional assays on solid media require up to 8 weeks for observations.
source: Conventional assays on solid media provide crude growth analysis, including antibiotic sensitivity, on large populations of cells but require up to 8 weeks for observations whereas specialized microfluidic methods require approximately 9 days (Choi et al., 2014; Barr et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Choi et al., 2014 and Barr et al., 2016.

claim: Specialized microfluidic methods require approximately 9 days for observations.
source: Conventional assays on solid media provide crude growth analysis, including antibiotic sensitivity, on large populations of cells but require up to 8 weeks for observations whereas specialized microfluidic methods require approximately 9 days (Choi et al., 2014; Barr et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Choi et al., 2014 and Barr et al., 2016.

claim: ODELAM can assay growth on up to ~100,000 colony forming units (CFUs) in a single experiment.
source: ODELAM bridges these disparate methods by assaying growth temporally at a mesoscale, on up to ~100,000 colony forming units (CFUs) in a single experiment.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the ODELAM method described by the authors.

claim: ODELAM was originally designed for yeast.
source: Originally designed for yeast, the adaptation offers improvements on phenotypic analysis and diagnostics for detecting and characterizing populations of drug resistant Mtb (Herricks et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Herricks et al., 2017.

claim: H37Rv had a median lag time of 0.5 hrs.
source: For example, H37Rv, an Mtb strain commonly used in research laboratories, had a median lag time of 0.5 s and grew with a doubling time median of 22.9 hrs (IQR 7.8).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: H37Rv grew with a doubling time median of 22.9 hrs (IQR 7.8).
source: For example, H37Rv, an Mtb strain commonly used in research laboratories, had a median lag time of 0.5 s and grew with a doubling time median of 22.9 hrs (IQR 7.8).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: H37Rv bacilli grew in exponential phase for a median of 52.5 hrs (IQR 33.8).
source: H37Rv bacilli grew in exponential phase for a median of 52.5 hrs (IQR 33.8) and during this time underwent a median of 3.1 doublings (IQR 1.6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: H37Rv underwent a median of 3.1 doublings (IQR 1.6).
source: H37Rv bacilli grew in exponential phase for a median of 52.5 hrs (IQR 33.8) and during this time underwent a median of 3.1 doublings (IQR 1.6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 1.

claim: H37Rv growth data are consistent with bulk laboratory measurements.
source: These data are consistent with bulk laboratory measurements (Peñuelas-Urquides et al., 2013) and demonstrate the innate heterogeneity of the genetically homogeneous clonal population.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Peñuelas-Urquides et al., 2013.

claim: H37Rv is sensitive to ofloxacin with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.5 μg/ml.
source: H37Rv is sensitive to ofloxacin with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.5 μg/ml as measured by normalized population growth in a standard dose-response curve (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: H37Rv initially grows at all concentrations of OFX indicating that OFX's toxicity does not alter growth kinetics over the first 24 hrs.
source: By ODELAM, we observed H37Rv to initially grow at all concentrations of OFX indicating that OFX's toxicity does not alter growth kinetics over the first 24 hrs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: OFX's mechanism of action on DNA gyrase leads to the accumulation of DNA damage.
source: This is consistent with OFX's mechanism of action on the enzyme target, DNA gyrase, which leads to the accumulation of DNA damage (Manjunatha et al., 2002; Gore et al., 2006; Willmott et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on OFX mechanism.

claim: The primary effect of OFX as detected by ODELAM was to arrest H37Rv growth after 2–3 doublings at the MIC.
source: Overall, the primary effect of OFX as detected by ODELAM was to arrest H37Rv growth after 2–3 doublings at the MIC and by the first doubling at high drug concentrations, while not appreciably affecting the rate at which H37Rv doubles prior to growth arrest (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 and Figure 2.

claim: TRS10 contains a missense mutation in the gene encoding gyrase A (D94G) that increases the isolate's MIC to OFX.
source: We observed a cultured clinical isolate TRS10, which contains a missense mutation in the gene encoding gyrase A (D94G) that increases the isolate's MIC to OFX (Eilertson et al., 2016; Hooper, 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eilertson et al., 2016 and Hooper, 2001.

claim: The median doubling time of TRS10 was approximately 20% longer than that of H37Rv in the absence of drug pressure.
source: In the absence of drug pressure, the median doubling time of TRS10 was approximately 20% longer than that of H37Rv (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: The MIC of TRS10 to OFX was 16 μg/ml as measured by the normalized population growth in a standard dose-response curve.
source: The MIC of TRS10 to OFX was 16 μg/ml as measured by the normalized population growth in a standard dose-response curve (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: TRS10 slowed its doubling time as OFX concentration increased up to, and including, its MIC.
source: By contrast to H37Rv, which ceased to grow at its MIC, TRS10 slowed its doubling time as OFX concentration increased up to, and including, its MIC (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: TRS10's doubling time slowed dramatically from ~30 to~50 hrs as drug concentration shifted from 2 to 4 μg/ml.
source: Further, TRS10's doubling time slowed dramatically from ~30 to~50 hrs as drug concentration shifted from 2 to 4 μg/ml (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: For H37Rv, the effect size for time in exponential phase tracked with the number of doublings as the concentration of OFX increased above 0.5 μg/ml.
source: For H37Rv, the effect size for time in exponential phase tracked with the number of doublings as the concentration of OFX increased above 0.5 μg/ml while doubling time and lag time effect sizes did not (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: For TRS10 the effect size for doubling time tracked with the number of doublings as the concentration of OFX increased.
source: In contrast, for TRS10 the effect size for doubling time tracked with the number of doublings as the concentration of OFX increased (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The OFX effect on TRS10's doubling time as opposed to the cessation of growth observed for H37Rv likely reflects the reduced binding of OFX to the mutant gyrase.
source: This OFX effect on TRS10's doubling time as opposed to the cessation of growth observed for H37Rv (T-Exp) likely reflects the reduced binding of OFX to the mutant gyrase (Maruri et al., 2012; Willmott et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Maruri et al., 2012 and Willmott et al., 1994, and inference from experimental data.

claim: Heteroresistance in cultured clinical isolates is prevalent and confounds diagnosis and treatment of Mtb.
source: Heteroresistance in cultured clinical isolates is prevalent and confounds diagnosis and treatment of Mtb (Sebastian et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Sebastian et al., 2017.

claim: ODELAM detected a single OFX resistant CFU from the 0.04% TRS10 mixture.
source: In this ODELAM assay, a single OFX resistant CFU was detected from the 0.04% TRS10 mixture (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The 50% mix detected 200 resistant CFUs out a total of 721 CFUs.
source: The 50% mix detected 200 resistant CFUs out a total of 721 CFUs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the heteroresistance detection experiments.

claim: 28 of 970 CFUs were detected in the 6.25% TRS10 mix.
source: Similarly, 28 of 970 CFUs were detected in the 6.25% TRS10 mix, and 12 of 1144 were detected in the 1.56% TRS10 mix (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 12 of 1144 CFUs were detected in the 1.56% TRS10 mix.
source: Similarly, 28 of 970 CFUs were detected in the 6.25% TRS10 mix, and 12 of 1144 were detected in the 1.56% TRS10 mix (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The relationship between dilution and detection was linear from 50% to 0.2%.
source: The relationship between dilution and detection was linear from 50% to 0.2%.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ODELAM consistently observed fewer resistant TRS10 CFUs from the mixture than expected from the OD600 measurements used to generate the mixture.
source: ODELAM consistently observed fewer resistant TRS10 CFUs from the mixture than expected from the OD600 measurements used to generate the mixture (Figure 5B) and likely reflects the vagaries associated with using OD600 to predict CFUs, which is known to vary between strains (Peñuelas-Urquides et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and citation to Peñuelas-Urquides et al., 2013.

claim: Clinical isolate ADB42 was previously observed to be OFX resistant with MIC ranging between 8 and 256 μg/ml of OFX.
source: Clinical isolate ADB42 was previously observed to be OFX resistant with MIC ranging between 8 and 256 μg/ml of OFX (Eilertson et al., 2016; Eilertson et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eilertson et al., 2016 and Eilertson et al., 2014.

claim: The canonical OFX resistance conferring gyrase-A D94G SNP was not present at a frequency sufficient to be associated with the observed OFX resistance in ADB42 by whole genome sequence analysis.
source: By whole genome sequence analysis, the canonical OFX resistance conferring gyrase-A D94G SNP was not present at a frequency sufficient to be associated with the observed OFX resistance; other mechanisms were attributed to the observed phenotype (Eilertson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Eilertson et al., 2016.

claim: The standard dose-response assay yielded a MIC of 16 μg/ml for ADB42.
source: In our hands, the standard dose-response assay yielded a MIC of 16 μg/ml (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: ADB42 was grown in culture and subjected to transcriptome analysis by RNA-sequencing, which revealed the presence of a gyrase-A D94G SNP at a frequency of 15%.
source: ADB42 was grown in culture and subjected to transcriptome analysis by RNA-sequencing, which revealed the presence of a gyrase-A D94G SNP at a frequency of 15% (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: ODELAM measured roughly 24% of the ADB42 CFUs were resistant to OFX.
source: Across the experiments reported here, ODELAM measured roughly 24% of the ADB42 CFUs were resistant to OFX, which is within a 95% confidence interval of random sampling modeled by a binomial distribution (Table 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: Thirty-three clones of ADB42 exhibited OFX resistance at 2 μg/ml OFX in both spot assay and ODELAM.
source: Thirty-three clones exhibited OFX resistance at 2 μg/ml OFX in both assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cloning experiments shown in Figure 8.

claim: Individual clones of ADB42 did not display phenotypic heterogeneity by ODELAM.
source: In contrast to the parental cultured clinical isolate, these individual clones did not display phenotypic heterogeneity by ODELAM (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from ODELAM analysis of clones.

claim: All 10 resistant isolates of ADB42 contained a SNP A7582G in gyrA, which corresponds to the canonical D94G mutations that confers OFX resistance.
source: All 10 resistant isolates contained a SNP A7582G in gyrA, which corresponds to the canonical D94G mutations that confers OFX resistance (Willmott et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data and citation to Willmott et al., 1994.

claim: The four sensitive clones of ADB42 did not contain the D94G SNP.
source: The four sensitive clones did not contain this SNP (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data presented in Table 3.

claim: After Mtb growth arrest on OFX, some cells appear to lyse as detected by a change in contrast.
source: After Mtb growth arrest on OFX, some cells appear to lyse as detected by a change in contrast (Figure 10A), which we interpret as a consequence of cytotoxicity (Figure 10A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 10A.

claim: The percentage of colonies that have the lysis phenotype increased with OFX concentration and became apparent at concentrations greater than 0.5 μg/ml OFX.
source: The percentage of colonies that have this phenotype increased with OFX concentration and became apparent at concentrations greater than 0.5 μg/ml OFX.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10.

claim: H37Rv showed as much as 95% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis.
source: Here H37Rv showed as much as 95% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis, where as ADB42 and TRS10 showed 65% and 30%, respectively (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: ADB42 showed 65% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis.
source: Here H37Rv showed as much as 95% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis, where as ADB42 and TRS10 showed 65% and 30%, respectively (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: TRS10 showed 30% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis.
source: Here H37Rv showed as much as 95% of the tracked colonies exhibiting cell lysis, where as ADB42 and TRS10 showed 65% and 30%, respectively (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: In the case of H37Rv, which, in the presence of OFX, exits exponential phase after ~20 hrs, ODELAM can detect drug sensitivity in ~30 hrs.
source: In the case of H37Rv, which, in the presence of OFX, exits exponential phase after ~20 hrs, ODELAM can detect drug sensitivity in ~30 hrs (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and convergence analysis in Figure 12.

claim: The time required to reliably determine the set of kinetic parameters for a growth curve must be ~1.5 times longer than the time needed for a CFU to exit exponential phase.
source: Using this routine, we calculated that the time required to reliably determine the set of kinetic parameters for a growth curve must be ~1.5 times longer than the time needed for a CFU to exit exponential phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 12.

claim: Fluoroquinolones such as OFX bind to gyrase and trap the enzyme-DNA complex in an intermediate state.
source: Fluoroquinolones such as OFX bind to gyrase and trap the enzyme-DNA complex in an intermediate state (Willmott et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Willmott et al., 1994.

claim: The trapped complex can stall RNA transcription and prevent progression of the replication fork.
source: The trapped complex can stall RNA transcription and prevent progression of the replication fork (Willmott et al., 1994; Gore et al., 2006; Shea and Hiasa, 1999; Manjunatha et al., 2002; Hiasa et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature on fluoroquinolone mechanism.

claim: In the presence of OFX, double stranded breaks in the DNA template free the RNA transcription complex and accumulate over time contributing to toxicity and cell death.
source: In the presence of OFX, double stranded breaks in the DNA template free the RNA transcription complex and accumulate over time contributing to toxicity and cell death (Willmott et al., 1994; Hiasa et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Willmott et al., 1994 and Hiasa et al., 1996.

claim: Even at OFX concentrations above the MIC (0.5 μg/ml), H37Rv continues to grow before they arrest synchronously after ~20 hrs.
source: Accordingly, even at OFX concentrations above the MIC (0.5 μg/ml), H37Rv continues to grow before they arrest synchronously after ~20 hrs (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Most H37Rv cells remain metabolically active and synthesize protein until drug-induced damage accumulates and growth stops.
source: We interpret this to mean that most cells remain metabolically active and synthesize protein until drug-induced damage accumulates and growth stops (Wang et al., 2009; Da Re et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by citations to Wang et al., 2009 and Da Re et al., 2009.

claim: Standard microwell plate MIC assays and indicator tube assays are sensitive and robust methods for detecting antimicrobial resistant Mtb.
source: Standard microwell plate MIC assays and indicator tube assays are sensitive and robust methods for detecting antimicrobial resistant Mtb; however, these bulk assays give little information on the presence of sub-populations that differ in their sensitivity to drugs (Lawson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lawson et al., 2013.

claim: Bulk assays give little information on the presence of sub-populations that differ in their sensitivity to drugs.
source: Standard microwell plate MIC assays and indicator tube assays are sensitive and robust methods for detecting antimicrobial resistant Mtb; however, these bulk assays give little information on the presence of sub-populations that differ in their sensitivity to drugs (Lawson et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lawson et al., 2013.

claim: ODELAM can discriminate individual CFUs with a sensitivity of roughly 1 in 1000.
source: This was validated with an artificially mixed population and was used to detect heteroresistance in a cultured clinical isolate, ADB42. In the mixed population ODELAM discriminates individual CFUs with a sensitivity of roughly 1 in 1000.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the heteroresistance detection experiments.

claim: ODELAM's sensitivity is dependent on the number of CFUs observed.
source: This level of precision is dependent on the number of CFUs observed and improvements in microscope optics, computation, and media preparation could increase this sensitivity by orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the method's capabilities.

claim: ODELAM could observe the rare but critical events that lead to development of drug resistance including individual persistent cells that go on to acquire drug resistance through mutation.
source: Thus, this approach could observe the rare but critical events that lead to development of drug resistance including individual persistent cells that go on to acquire drug resistance through mutation (Cohen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future capabilities, supported by citation to Cohen et al., 2013.

claim: For concentrations of OFX up to and including 16 times the MIC, there was no measurable effect on H37Rv's growth rate until growth ceased.
source: Remarkably, for concentrations of OFX up to and including 16 times the MIC, there was no measurable effect on H37Rv's growth rate until growth ceased.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from ODELAM measurements.

claim: OFX had a measurable effect on growth rate of TRS10 well below its MIC.
source: By contrast OFX had a measurable effect on growth rate of TRS10 well below its MIC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from ODELAM measurements.

claim: These differences in OFX effects reflect the differential accumulation of cytotoxic molecular intermediates due to differences in the ability of the drug to bind the different variants of gyrase.
source: We interpret these differences to reflect the differential accumulation of cytotoxic molecular intermediates due to differences in the ability of the drug to bind the different variants of gyrase.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on experimental observations and knowledge of drug mechanism.

claim: ODELAM is not restricted to Mtb and can be adapted to any colony forming microorganism.
source: ODELAM is not restricted to Mtb and can be adapted to any colony forming microorganism.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the method's broader applicability.

claim: ODELAM can observe up to 1500 CFUs in each region of interest.
source: In each region of interest, ODELAM can observe up to 1500 CFUs and quantify their morphological and multiparameter growth phenotypes.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the ODELAM method.

claim: A typical ODELAM experiment involves 80 or 96 regions of interest.
source: A typical experiment involves 80 or 96 regions of interest.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the ODELAM method.

claim: Mtb bacilli were observed to grow immediately after spotting on media.
source: In these experiments, Mtb bacilli were observed to grow immediately after spotting on media.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments.

claim: Mtb CFUs were recorded for a total of 96 hrs.
source: Mtb CFUs were recorded for a total of 96 hrs and growth curves were extracted from the projected area of the individual colonies over time and fitted to the Gompertz function (Figure 1B; Herricks et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: Growth curves were fitted to the Gompertz function.
source: Mtb CFUs were recorded for a total of 96 hrs and growth curves were extracted from the projected area of the individual colonies over time and fitted to the Gompertz function (Figure 1B; Herricks et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method, with citation to Herricks et al., 2017.

claim: The kinetic parameters doubling time (Td), lag time (T-Lag), time in exponential phase (T-Exp) and number of doublings (Num Dbl) were derived from the Gompertz function.
source: The kinetic parameters doubling time (Td), lag time (T-Lag), time in exponential phase (T-Exp) and number of doublings (Num Dbl) were derived from the Gompertz function and plotted as normalized frequency histograms which revealed population distributions (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method.

claim: ODELAM demonstrates the innate heterogeneity of the genetically homogeneous clonal population.
source: These data are consistent with bulk laboratory measurements (Peñuelas-Urquides et al., 2013) and demonstrate the innate heterogeneity of the genetically homogeneous clonal population.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing variation in growth parameters.

claim: Above the MIC, OFX toxicity led to cessation of growth, detected as an exit from exponential phase.
source: Above the MIC, toxicity led to cessation of growth, detected as an exit from exponential phase.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments.

claim: Narrowing of the population histograms reflects a more uniform population.
source: Narrowing of the population histograms reflects a more uniform population.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the histogram data.

claim: The doubling time distributions did not appreciably change with OFX treatment in H37Rv.
source: Notably, the doubling time distributions did not appreciably change; cells maintained similar doubling rates prior to growth cessation.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: H37Rv cells maintained similar doubling rates prior to growth cessation.
source: Notably, the doubling time distributions did not appreciably change; cells maintained similar doubling rates prior to growth cessation.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments.

claim: TRS10 grew continuously over a 96 hrs time period at its MIC OFX concentration of 16 μg/ml.
source: By contrast TRS10 grew continuously over a 96 hrs time period at its MIC OFX concentration of 16 μg/ml.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Before growth arrest at its MIC, the doubling rate of H37Rv slowed slightly.
source: Before growth arrest at its MIC, the doubling rate of H37Rv slowed slightly, whereas the doubling rate for TRS10 slowed considerably and at a population level exhibited a broad spread of doubling times.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments.

claim: The doubling rate for TRS10 slowed considerably and at a population level exhibited a broad spread of doubling times.
source: Before growth arrest at its MIC, the doubling rate of H37Rv slowed slightly, whereas the doubling rate for TRS10 slowed considerably and at a population level exhibited a broad spread of doubling times.
evidence: This is an observation from ODELAM experiments.

claim: The mechanisms of action for OFX toxicity are different between H37Rv and TRS10.
source: This suggests that the mechanisms of action for OFX toxicity are different between the two strains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the different growth phenotypes observed.

claim: As the concentration of OFX is increased in TRS10, off-target effects begin to manifest, which alter growth in a pleotropic manner resulting in the observed broadening of the doubling time of the population.
source: Thus, as the concentration of OFX is increased, off-target effects begin to manifest, which alter growth in a pleotropic manner resulting in the observed broadening of the doubling time of the population (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Inhibition of DNA gyrase in H37Rv likely results in the accumulation of replication and transcription intermediates, leading to the more uniform population distribution observed.
source: By contrast, inhibition of DNA gyrase in H37Rv likely results in the accumulation of replication and transcription intermediates, leading to the more uniform population distribution observed.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The standard dose-response batch culture MIC assay yielded inaccurate results for heteroresistant mixtures.
source: Thus, the standard dose-response batch culture MIC assay yielded inaccurate results and was unable to reflect the MIC of the constituent population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The standard dose-response batch culture MIC assay was unable to reflect the MIC of the constituent population in heteroresistant mixtures.
source: Thus, the standard dose-response batch culture MIC assay yielded inaccurate results and was unable to reflect the MIC of the constituent population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ODELAM directly observed OFX resistant CFUs in the mixed culture.
source: By contrast ODELAM directly observed OFX resistant CFUs in the mixed culture (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Resistant and sensitive CFUs were distinguished by their number of doublings and their growth in exponential phase.
source: Resistant and sensitive CFUs were distinguished by their number of doublings and their growth in exponential phase.
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method used in ODELAM.

claim: The observed MIC varied across the dilution series, increasing with the proportion of resistant cells.
source: The observed MIC varied across the dilution series, increasing with the proportion of resistant cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the MIC assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The standard MIC assay is sufficiently sensitive to detect shifts in the MIC at very low relative concentrations of resistant cells.
source: While the assay is sufficiently sensitive to detect shifts in the MIC at very low relative concentrations of resistant cells, it does not distinguish between a monoculture with a specific resistance phenotype and a mixed population with heteroresistance.
evidence: This is an observation from the MIC assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The standard MIC assay does not distinguish between a monoculture with a specific resistance phenotype and a mixed population with heteroresistance.
source: While the assay is sufficiently sensitive to detect shifts in the MIC at very low relative concentrations of resistant cells, it does not distinguish between a monoculture with a specific resistance phenotype and a mixed population with heteroresistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Below 0.2% TRS10 in the mixture, the expected number of TRS10 CFUs fall to around 1 to 5 in 1000 individuals.
source: Below 0.2% the expected number of TRS10 CFUs fall to around 1 to 5 in 1000 individuals and because each region of interest observes about 1000 CFUs, the measurements become dominated by chance.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the experimental design.

claim: Each region of interest observes about 1000 CFUs.
source: Below 0.2% the expected number of TRS10 CFUs fall to around 1 to 5 in 1000 individuals and because each region of interest observes about 1000 CFUs, the measurements become dominated by chance.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the ODELAM method.
